items.followUp: What is meant by an ideal machine, and what is its efficiency?

rubric.why: An ideal system is defined by the absence of energy loss.
rubric.description: States that an ideal system has no energy loss.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the no-loss condition.

rubric.why: In an ideal system, all input work is transferred as output work.
rubric.description: States that output work equals input work, or that efficiency is 100%.

modelAnswer: An ideal system is one in which there is no loss of energy, such as loss due to friction.
In an ideal system, output work equals input work and its efficiency is 100%.

items.followUp: What is the SI unit of work, and how is one joule defined?

rubric.why: The watt is the SI unit of power.
rubric.description: Names the watt (W) as the unit of power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the unit.

rubric.why: One watt is the rate of doing one joule of work in one second.
rubric.description: Defines one watt as one joule per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second (1 W = 1 J/s).

items.followUp: A 4 kg block rests on a horizontal surface. If the coefficient of friction is 0.25, calculate the frictional force. Take g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: The mass and coefficient of friction are the given data needed for the calculation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both given values.

rubric.why: Friction is calculated from the coefficient of friction and the normal reaction; on a horizontal floor, R = mg.
rubric.description: Uses F = μR and R = mg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relations.

rubric.why: The normal reaction is the block's weight on the horizontal floor.
rubric.description: Calculates the normal reaction as 50 N using g = 10 m/s².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct normal reaction with unit.

rubric.why: Substituting the normal reaction into F = μR gives 30 N.
rubric.description: Shows the friction-force substitution and calculation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct substitution leading to 30 N.

rubric.why: The calculated frictional force must be stated with its unit.
rubric.description: Gives the frictional force as 30 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 5 kg, μ = 0.6; take g = 10 m/s².
For a horizontal floor, normal reaction R = mg.
Answer: The force of friction is 30 N.
